concepts.def: One person who owns the business
2+ people who own a business together
Owner is liable for all debts
Working for yourself, not an employer

walkthroughs.body_html:
A sole trader is one self-employed person.

Examples: a window cleaner, a hairdresser, a market trader.

Pros: easy to start, you keep all profit.
Cons: unlimited liability — your home could pay business debts. 😬

A partnership is 2–20 owners working together.

Examples: a vet practice, a law firm.

Partners share workload, ideas and profit — but also debts.

Compare:

  • Sole trader — full control, full risk.
  • Partnership — shared brain, shared debt.

A good deed of partnership writes down who does what and how profit is split. 📜
